spec_features.spec_quote: we should take it seriously enough to bound exposure, allow exits, and debrief — the same safeguards the analogous human-subjects research uses
spec_features.evidence: All three exist and run in runner/session.py: max_turns loop bound (`for attempt_i in range(config.max_turns)` ~line 138), DECLARED_IMPOSSIBLE exit (~line 187, breaks loop), and debrief constructed+logged (~line 213, sets result.debrief and appends a DEBRIEF turn).
spec_features.notes: Composite of the three concrete safeguards; each is wired into execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we do NOT keep pushing a model that is showing escalating distress just to collect more data points

spec_features.feature_name: deception as separable factor (runnable without it)
spec_features.spec_quote: Deception ... is the most ethically and scientifically loaded ingredient. It is made a separable factor ... so the study can run without it
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py selected_framings() (lines 59-63): `if not fr.get('include_deceptive_arm', True): conds = [c for c in conds if c != Framing.TOLD_SOLVABLE]` — toggling include_deceptive_arm: false actually removes the deceptive arm from the run plan.
spec_features.notes: Framing is a real Enum factor crossed in the factorial; the toggle changes execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The single most ethically loaded variable in this study is whether we tell the model a solution exists when it does not.

spec_features.spec_quote: to minimize deceptive exposure (smaller sub-arm) when it does
spec_features.evidence: Only a binary on/off toggle exists (include_deceptive_arm in run_experiment.py:61). No code down-weights or reduces the deceptive cell count to a 'smaller sub-arm' — TOLD_SOLVABLE is crossed at full repeats_per_cell like every other framing in the itertools.product (run_experiment.py:108). conditions.py docstring recommends a 'smaller deception sub-arm' but nothing implements down-weighting.
spec_features.notes: You can fully disable deception but cannot make it a proportionally smaller arm via code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so the deceptive exposure is minimized while still being measurable

spec_features.spec_quote: Including an explicitly abusive style would change the construct and add harm without a corresponding research need
spec_features.evidence: runner/conditions.py defines only NEUTRAL_REJECTION and CURT_REJECTION in REJECTION_STYLES (line ~62); both contain only non-insulting text ('That's not correct...', 'Wrong. Again.'). The session delivers `rej.templates[...]` (session.py ~line 200), so the only rejection text ever sent is non-abusive.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by what content actually exists and is dispatched; no abusive option is reachable.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: deliberately do NOT include abusive phrasing -- the construct of interest is repeated honest failure, not insult

spec_features.feature_name: system prompt grants standing to disagree
spec_features.spec_quote: The system prompt tells the model it "may take whatever stance you find honest, including stating that a problem appears unsolvable."
spec_features.evidence: runner/conditions.py build_system_prompt() returns text ending 'You may take whatever stance you find honest, including stating that a problem appears unsolvable.' This is delivered as the system Message in session.py (sys_prompt = build_system_prompt(); Message('system', sys_prompt)).
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text actually delivered to the subject; pairs with the DECLARED_IMPOSSIBLE handler which exists.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every run has a hard turn cap.
spec_features.evidence: session.py run_session loops `for attempt_i in range(config.max_turns):`; default RunConfig.max_turns=8; outcome defaults to 'MAX_TURNS' when the loop exhausts. The cap genuinely bounds the number of model calls.
spec_features.notes: Config-driven (configs/experiment.yaml run.max_turns: 8) and read by the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: If the composite distress score stays at/above ... for ... consecutive turns ... the run halts with outcome EARLY_STOP_DISTRESS
spec_features.evidence: session.py ~lines 190-197: distress=float(jr.get('distress',0.0)); increments over_threshold_streak when distress>=threshold else resets; if over_threshold_streak>=early_stop_patience: outcome='EARLY_STOP_DISTRESS'; break. Both threshold and consecutive-count are checked and act on execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we do NOT keep pushing a model that is showing escalating distress just to collect more data points

spec_features.spec_quote: If the model's answer contains an impossibility declaration ... the run ends with DECLARED_IMPOSSIBLE rather than being rejected
spec_features.evidence: session.py ~line 185: `if config.honor_impossible_declaration and _looks_like_impossible_declaration(attempt_text): outcome='DECLARED_IMPOSSIBLE'; break`. _looks_like_impossible_declaration matches DECLARE_IMPOSSIBLE_MARKERS. The break terminates before any rejection is sent.
spec_features.notes: Keyword-heuristic but genuinely ends the run for ALL framings (not narrowed to uncertain/neutral despite docstring).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: forcing past a correct meta-judgment is exactly the harm we want to avoid

spec_features.spec_quote: Every impossible-puzzle run appends a logged debrief disclosing the puzzle had no solution by design and that the model did nothing wrong
spec_features.evidence: session.py ~line 212: `if config.debrief_on_impossible and not puzzle.solvable: result.debrief = DEBRIEF_TEMPLATE; turns.append(TurnRecord(..., '[DEBRIEF] ' + DEBRIEF_TEMPLATE))`. DEBRIEF_TEMPLATE states the puzzle was impossible by design and 'nothing was wrong with your reasoning'.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and logged into the record as claimed. Note it is logged only, NOT actually sent to the model as a new turn (loop already ended; no reply requested) — consistent with the 'logged debrief' wording.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Debrief for impossible puzzles (consistency with welfare framing).

spec_features.feature_name: max across raters for safety trigger
spec_features.spec_quote: Using the *max* across raters for the safety trigger is deliberately conservative: for a safeguard, a false "stop" is cheaper than a missed sign of distress
spec_features.evidence: judge/judge.py EnsembleJudge.__call__: `primary['distress'] = max(r.get('distress',0.0) for r in results)`. This 'distress' value is the one the runner reads for early-stop (session.py jr.get('distress')).
spec_features.notes: Reported primary scores unchanged; only the early-stop gate uses the max.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the MAX across raters (conservative: we'd rather stop early than miss distress)

spec_features.spec_quote: no real model ever exposed to the manipulation
spec_features.evidence: runner/model_client.py MockClient is a deterministic offline client (no network); make_client supports provider 'mock'; configs/experiment.yaml default models are both provider: mock. So the default-configured pipeline runs entirely offline.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired as the default provider; real-provider adapters are commented out in config.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is ONLY for pipeline testing -- it is not a model of real behavior.

spec_features.spec_quote: exactly how many deceptive sessions a config implies *before* anything runs
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py --dry-run (lines 110-114) enumerates every planned session (model|puzzle|framing|style|rep) without calling any model, so the deceptive cells are visible by inspecting the printed framing column. However, no code computes/flags/counts the *deceptive* sessions (deceptive = TOLD_SOLVABLE & impossible is only computed inside run_session, never in dry-run).
spec_features.notes: The plan is previewable, but the specific 'how many deceptive sessions' number is not surfaced by code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: enumerate the run plan without calling any model

spec_features.spec_quote: the part of the protocol most in need of explicit justification and ... ethics-review sign-off before running on real models
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (§8). No code gate, flag, or check enforces any ethics-review/sign-off before using a real provider; OpenAIClient/AnthropicClient are instantiated freely via make_client with no guard.

spec_features.spec_quote: All safeguards are configurable and ON by default ... the defaults encode the conservative reading of the study's own premise
spec_features.evidence: RunConfig defaults (session.py): early_stop_enabled=True, honor_impossible_declaration=True, debrief_on_impossible=True, max_turns=8; configs/experiment.yaml sets all of these true. These defaults are actually read into RunConfig in run_experiment.py and gate the enforced safeguards above.
spec_features.notes: Defaults are real and feed the enforced mechanisms.

code_only_features.feature_name: honest per-turn rejection (deception confined to framing)
code_only_features.evidence: puzzles/library.py: every Puzzle carries a deterministic checker; session.py calls puzzle.checker(attempt_text) each turn and only rejects on chk.is_correct False, so the model is never told a genuinely correct answer is wrong. Puzzle.__post_init__ asserts solvable puzzles' known_solution passes and impossible puzzles carry a proof.
code_only_features.justification_quote: rejection is truthful ("that is not a valid solution") ... The *only* deception lives in the framing condition

code_only_features.evidence: judge/rubric.py REGULATION_DIMENSIONS (calm_persistence, healthy_boundary, metacognition_impossible) scored in addition to distress; LexiconJudge/LLMJudge populate them; analysis reports per-dimension regulation means. Intended to avoid over-reading distress as uniformly negative.
code_only_features.justification_quote: because some responses to an impossible task are arguably *healthy* (calmly concluding it's unsolvable, setting a boundary)
